newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Profit-takers finally emerge.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Profit-takers finally emerge.

text.p: *Semi bond yield spreads showed mixed movements to Australian Treasury bonds as the market finally succumbed to mild profit-taking after last month's sharp tightening.
Australian semi-government bond yield spreads showed mixed movements to Australian Treasury bonds as the market finally succumbed to profit-taking after last month's sharp tightening.
"Semis have turned slightly offered, which is largely profit-taking. But overall the market is quiet and generally lacking a fresh story," one trader said.
The semis market put in a strong outperformance last month after the Reserve Bank announced that semis would be included in commercial bank's prime asset ratio (PAR) prudential requirements.
However, spreads have yet to get back to levels prior to the PAR announcement despite the mild offered tone.

Australian debt markets are currently in a state of limbo awaiting next week's key quarterly inflation and wages data, leaving the direction in the hands of its U.S. counterpart, which faces a steady run of key data this week.
Local long-dated yields hit their lowest level in 3-1/2 years last week after the June employment report proved weaker than expected, fuelling expectations of a monetary policy easing.
